That's a fair point, and I'll own that I was stating my preference pretty strongly. You're right that it's not one-size-fits-all — some people genuinely thrive on in-person collaboration, and there are real benefits to being around colleagues, especially for newer employees who need mentorship.

But I don't want to fully water down what I actually think, either. I'd say it like this: remote work tends to suit me and a lot of people I've observed, but both approaches have genuine merits and it really depends on the person, the team, and the kind of work. My frustration is more with blanket one-size-fits-all mandates in either direction, rather than with offices themselves.
